info.name: Ecommerce API - Full Application
info.description:
Manual tests for the project API. The main flow covers registration, login, products, the cart, orders, shipping, and delivery, with permissions and inventory checks.

Set baseUrl in Variables. Sign in as an admin in folder 00 using adminEmail and adminPassword, or paste the JWT into adminToken without the Bearer prefix. Run folders 00 through 04 in order. Requests automatically save tokens and IDs. If test data is missing, requests still run so you can inspect Laravel's response.

Set the project root as the Postman working directory. Select postman/fixtures/product.png or postman/fixtures/not-an-image.txt when a file request requires it.

Folder 05 covers additional security checks and the login rate limit. Run folders 06 through 08 manually on a test database, following the request descriptions. These scenarios stop a service or introduce temporary faults. Known-issue tests describe the expected behavior and can fail on the current code.

To repeat the full flow, return to 00 and 01 to create new customers and products. Cancellation, shipping, and rerun scenarios create records in the test database.

request.description:
Click Send once. The visible request checks /health, then the post-response script sends two POST /orders requests together. Open Test Results and the Postman Console to see the responses. Expect 201 and 409 in either order.

For server-side concurrency, set baseUrl2 to a second Laravel instance using the same MySQL database, inventory service, and JWT_SECRET. With the local Docker setup, open a second PowerShell window in the project root and run:

    docker compose run --rm --no-deps --name ecommerce2026-race-app -p 127.0.0.1:8001:8000 app

Set baseUrl2 to http://127.0.0.1:8001. Leave the window running through the concurrency test, then stop it with Ctrl+C. If baseUrl2 is empty, both requests go to baseUrl and the default single-process server may handle them sequentially. To send the requests manually, open POST /orders in two tabs. Use registrationToken for customer A and productsCustomerToken for customer B as Bearer tokens, and send each request to a different instance. For manual cleanup, set raceWinnerOrderId to the successful order ID and set raceLoserToken and raceLoserItemId for the customer whose request failed.

request.description:
Run this command in PowerShell from the project root before clicking Send:

    docker compose stop inventory-service

Expect 503 with a clear message within a few seconds. Keep the service stopped for the next two requests.

Restart the service before clicking Send:

    docker compose start inventory-service

Wait for the new gRPC Server started message in docker compose logs -f --since 1m inventory-service. If you receive 503, retry the read after startup completes. Available stock remains at 2.

item.name: 07 Order Save Failure
item.description: Run this manual test on a test database. Complete the cart setup for customer C in 06 and restart inventory. Add a temporary MySQL trigger for customer C so that MySQL rejects the order insert after stock has been reserved.

item.name: Force MySQL to reject saving the order

request.description: Available stock should return to 2 after the order write fails. To verify that the reservation was created and released, open PostgreSQL with docker compose exec inventory-db psql -U inventory_user -d ecommerce_inventory. Replace PRODUCT_ID with faultProductId and run SELECT reservation_id, status FROM inventory_reservations WHERE product_id = PRODUCT_ID ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 1;. Expect RELEASED.

request.description: MySQL rolls back the transaction and leaves the cart intact.

item.name: 08 gRPC Deadline - Durable Checkout Recovery
item.description: Run only on disposable test databases after 06 with inventory online. Drop the MySQL trigger from 07 first. For deterministic manual steps, stop checkout-recovery temporarily; restart it after this scenario. A timeout preserves a durable checkout intent. Retrying resumes the original reservation instead of reserving twice.

item.name: Checkout when reservation exceeds the deadline
Verify checkout is pending and the cart is preserved

request.description: After the timeout, the cart remains intact with checkout_pending=true. A recovery worker may finish it automatically, so stop checkout-recovery during this manual scenario.

item.name: Verify one reservation backs the recovered order

request.description: The fixture began with two units and the recovered order contains one unit, so availability must be 1. PostgreSQL must show one ACTIVE reservation for this product matching the recovered MySQL order reservation_id, not two. Restart automatic recovery with docker compose up -d checkout-recovery.
